ProQuest queue with session recovery

2,765 orders · one request at a time · progress saved after every result.

Automatic session recovery

When ProQuest offers “Begin a new session,” the helper clicks it, chooses institutional access, and selects NYU Library. It then retries the same order once after ProQuest returns to its search page. It leaves isolated errors for review and pauses for unfamiliar screens, access challenges, or three consecutive failures. Do not press Back.

Only this queue’s download tab is controlled. The helper never reads or fills NYU credentials. If NYU asks you to sign in, complete that step yourself; the queue waits for a return to ProQuest.

First use
  1. Open this queue using the extension’s toolbar button in the Chrome browser where you are signed in to ProQuest through NYU.
  2. In Chrome PDF settings, select Download PDFs. Set its download location to your existing ProQuest Pre-1937 Orders folder and turn off “Ask where to save each file.”
  3. Choose that same folder below. The queue will check existing PDFs before requesting anything.
  4. Press Start / resume. Keep this page open and the computer awake. Allow its download tab and any Chrome download permission prompts.

Folder access is read-only. This page sends no files, credentials, or progress to a server. Requests use only the supplied PDF links. The helper can recognize ProQuest’s session controls. The queue pauses after two minutes without a PDF, or allows up to ten minutes for a recognized session recovery. A 12-second minimum between requests follows the setting in your original file; it is not a verified server limit.

No folder selected

Choose your download folder to begin. Downloads have not started.

Progress is saved in this browser. Export a checkpoint to move computers or keep a backup. On every resume, saved PDFs are checked again in the selected folder. Previous “done” ticks are not treated as evidence of a saved PDF.

If a request pauses

Inspect the download tab. Do not press Back: that can trigger the previous PDF again. If ProQuest asks you to sign in, sign in normally and return here. If it asks you to wait, leave the queue paused. Use “ProQuest error — pause now” to flag the current request for attention. Start / resume will leave that flagged order for later and continue with pending orders; “Retry on next start” explicitly enables a retry. A recognized session error allows one automatic recovery and retry for the current order. An isolated failed order is left for review; three consecutive failed orders pause the queue.

If ProQuest saved a PDF under an unexpected name, use “Associate saved PDF” on that order. Filename matching and PDF marker checks establish that a file was saved; you must still inspect its pages to confirm the order’s identity and completeness.
